blurb: This watercolour of a man in a rowing boat is very freely painted. The man is holding an oar pushing the boat onto the shore. It is likely this location is around the coast at Cap Martin. The figure is vigorously painted, and the sea, coastline and sky have been quickly depicted in washes of watercolour. This picture would not have taken Knighton-Hammond very long to paint.

title: Houses of Parliament
subject: Cityscape
blurb: This view of the Thames and the Houses of Parliament would have been painted soon after the artist’s move to London in 1900. Westminster Bridge divides the picture horizontally and beyond the picture become hazy – perhaps with smog. The barges on the slow moving Thames give a sense of movement which is further enhanced by the birds in flight.

title: Ombersley, Worcester
subject: Streetscape
blurb: The shepherd driving his sheep along a street in Ombersley, Worcestershire is colourful and freely painted. The vernacular buildings show good perspective as the streetscape recedes into the distance. The shepherd and sheep have little detail, but the good foreshortening give a sense of movement.

title: Street scene with sheep
subject: Streetscape
blurb: The shepherd driving his sheep has movement as they approach the spectator. The foreshortening adds to the effect. The red sandstone cottages with their thatched roofs have a historic feel and the human touch is added by the figure sitting on a bench by the front door. The artist, in this early picture, demonstrates his skill with aerial perspective.

title: Bakewell, Derbyshire
subject: Streetscape
blurb: This cottage in Bakewell, Derbyshire is painted to achieve the utmost charm. The horse and cart appear to be waiting outside the cottage for the owner. A fresh, colourful picture painted with freedom. The horse and cart show a good understanding of foreshortening.

title: Cortina
subject: Landscape
blurb: A view of Cortina at the foot of the Alps. The spectator’s eye is drawn from the local colours of the foreground into the range of buildings in the middle ground and onto the atmospheric distance and up to the mountain top. The figures and horse and rider give a sense of scale as they walk the road in front of the buildings. A fresh, colourful picture undertaken on one of the artist’s painting excursions soon after he arrived in Italy in 1922.

title: San Giorgio Maggiore, Venice
subject: Coastal Scene
blurb: This watercolour would have been painted soon after Knighton-Hammond arrived in Venice in 1922. A view of San Giorgio Maggiore across the Guidecca. The church was designed by Andrea Palladio and stands majestic in this most iconic city. The artist has rapidly painted the church, gondolas and their reflections in the water with a newfound freedom reminiscent of the Impressionists. He captures the light of Venice and the heat haze giving San Giorgio an atmospheric appearance.

title: Race meeting at Epsom
subject: Sporting Scene
blurb: Once again Knighton-Hammond was at Epsom positioned behind the scenes to produce this colourful watercolour. The vehicles, caravans and funfair have people milling around, one with horse but a workhorse rather than a racehorse. Toward the race circuit there are marquees and tents housing the entertainment. The stands in the background appear to be full of spectators. A typically busy and colourful picture of a subject dear to the artist.

title: Race meeting at Epsom
subject: Sporting Scene
blurb: The race meeting at Epsom is a typical behind the scenes view by Knighton-Hammond. His main focus for the composition is the modes of transport and accommodation in the form of colourful caravans and a car in the foreground. As one moves into the picture towards the race circuit there is a heightened feeling of anticipation as the spectators await the horses and jockeys at the finishing post. The artist goes to the trouble of even painting in the discarded rubbish in the immediate foreground. The picture overall is colourful and lively.

title: Dunster Castle
subject: Landscape
blurb: Dunster Castle may well have been painted whilst Knighton-Hammond was travelling the west country. The castle sits in the hillside amongst trees. The building, landscape and sky are very impressionistic with regards to the free brushstrokes, light and colour. These techniques would have been developed during the decade Knighton-Hammond spent in France and Italy.

title: Tractor in Haymaking Scene
subject: Landscape
blurb: A tractor in a haymaking scene is a busy picture with figures contributing to the task in hand. The figures have little definition and detail but one can immediately identify their place in the composition. The tractor dominates the picture with the driver appearing to look back at the spectator.

title: Cattle and trees in a landscape
subject: Landscape
blurb: Cattle and trees in a landscape is a colourful composition. Painted at speed, something Knighton-Hammond was well capable of doing even in later life. Painted with great freedom but still achieving the impressions required to make the picture work in terms of light, movement, spontaneity and aerial perspective.

title: Cattle in landscape with farm buildings
subject: Landscape
blurb: A freely executed watercolour of cattle in a landscape with farm buildings in the background. This style is Knighton-Hammond in his latter years. The farm would have been local to him at his studio and home at Higher Farm, Seaborough in Dorset. The cattle have little definition and the colour of the grass may not be too close to reality, but the picture works when viewed from a distance.

title: Sunshine on Brighton Beach
subject: Coastal Scene
blurb: Sunshine on Brighton Beach is a full and busy picture. Three figures are sitting amongst the many small sailing boats on the beach. The sea wall is in the middle ground and the buildings forming the streetscape are bathed in bright sunshine. The figures in the foreground may well have been family members. The artist has used colours to good effect creating an interest composition.

title: Henley Manor near Crewkerne
subject: Landscape
blurb: This picture of Henley Manor near Crewkerne in Somerset is dominated by the three large trees which divide up the scene. There are chickens in the foreground and a boy, possibly Knighton-Hammond’s son, John. Henley Manor and other buildings are in the background. One has the feeling that this picture was painted at speed with pure, direct watercolour.

title: The Horse Fair
subject: Landscape
blurb: Full of light, colour and air this watercolour of the horse fair is probably Ditchling. Knighton-Hammond wrote a treatise of watercolour painting and used the Village Horse Show at Ditchling as a case study. Firstly, he would sketch in charcoal the permanent features such as the trees. Next the figures and motor cars are sketched in outline in watercolour at lightning speed before they moved away followed by horses. The features that affect colour, form, light and shade are painted in. Splashes of colour were added as near to the shape of the shadows as possible; then the tents in the middle distance were drawn followed by the hills in the background and the sky. Once the colours forming the shadows were dry, he would complete the grass and foliage to the trees.

title: Returning from the Derby, 1901
subject: Sporting Scene
blurb: Returning from the Derby has figures appearing very dignified in their colourful Victorian/Edwardian attire at the Epsom race meeting. Coaches and horses are ferrying people from the race meeting. There are busy crowds of spectators and one can sense the hustle and bustle of the movement taking place. The stands form the background. A very busy, early picture.

title: Ascot, 1901
subject: Sporting Scene
blurb: A scene at Ascot towards the end of the race meeting. The figures appear very dignified in their Victorian/Edwardian attire as they move aside to allow the coach and horses through providing movement to the composition. The stands and the Surrey hills form the background. A very busy, early picture.

title: Group of Children
subject: Conversation Piece
blurb: This group of children would have been painted a great speed. There is an immediate feeling of human presence with each child having their own characteristics. With very little detailing each child would be recognisable. It would appear Knighton-Hammond sketched the outlines of the figure in a sepia wash before adding the facial features and clothing. A fun picture full of characters.

title: Farm buildings with figures
subject: Landscape
blurb: A farmhouse and attached farm buildings are freely painted in watercolour yet with very accurate perspective and detailing. The trees have a similar freedom of brushwork. The composition, as a whole, would have been painted in pure direct watercolour at great speed. The figures and handcart give scale and spontaneity. The roof tile contrast with the greens of the foliage and the blue and white of the sky.

title: Cathedral Interior
subject: Interior Scene
blurb: A very freely painted interior of a cathedral. The columns and pulpit appear to be of a red sandstone. The view down the nave have figures which give a sense of scale to this large vaulted interior.

title: Shepherd with flock in landscape
subject: Landscape
blurb: An extensive landscape with shepherd attending the flock of sheep. A dull day depicted in subdued colours. The local colours of green and brown contrast with the atmospheric colour of the blue in the background give depth to the picture.

title: Sailing Boat in Harbour
subject: Coastal Scene
blurb: This sailing boat in the harbour is both colourful and busy with figures. One of the figures is part way up the rigging either ascending or descending the mast. The buildings across the harbour are freely depicted in an impressionist manner part in sunshine and part in shadow.

title: River, Bridge and Mountains
subject: Landscape
blurb: This picture is dominated by the single arched bridge spanning the river and the maritime alps in the background. Using very few colours Knighton-Hammond has created a landscape composition of significant interest. There are a few trees either end of the bridge and along the river. The mountains are depicted in sunshine and shadow in a range of colours. There is an air of tranquillity and nature at its best.

title: Venice
subject: Streetscape
blurb: This scene of Venice has a blue, Mediterranean tint to it. The buildings and palaces running along the canal are painted with little detail but relying on the impression created by the freely painted watercolour. The gondolas give a sense of movement and scale to the composition.

title: The Royal Exchange, Manchester
subject: Streetscape
blurb: The Royal Exchange in Manchester appears to be undergoing building works with scaffolding and cranes in place. There is a workman going about his work on the roof of the portico and there are horses and carts in the street. The building is well observed with regards to perspective and this is continued in the streetscape. Knighton-Hammond was to use this watercolour from which to produce an etching.

title: Flower Study
subject: Flower Study
blurb: This flower study in watercolours has the strength and boldness of colour of an oil painting. The roses are three-dimensional created by the gradation of tone. As with the majority of Knighton-Hammond’s flower studies there is the odd flower on the table rather than neatly contained within the vase. He liked a less formal composition.

title: Flower Study
subject: Flower Study
blurb: The flower study features the blue vases which appear in many of Knighton-Hammond’s still life compositions. The flowers are painted in thick oil paint giving texture and three-dimensional qualities to the arrangement. The strong, bold colours make for a striking picture which one cannot ignore.

title: On the Lathkill
subject: Landscape
blurb: This valley is the Lathkill Dale in Derbyshire. The river draws the spectator’s eye to the small but quaint Fisherman’s Cottage with smoke coming from the chimney. An autumn scene with the leaves on the tree changing colour. The picture is given depth by the use of local and atmospheric colours. The river gives movement with reflections and the waterfall. The cattle give a sense of scale.

title: Flowers in the window
subject: Flower Study
blurb: A jug of flowers on the window sill was painted in oils. It is likely that the artist passing, liked the composition and painted it in its simple form. A colourful flower study.

title: The Gardener's Wife
subject: Portrait
blurb: The Gardener’s Wife, a Mrs Dutfield, appears a little awkward as she poses for her portrait on a sunny day. The artist loved painting portraits of people with character and the sitter has it in abundance and Knighton-Hammond conveys human presence rather than just artist process. The portrait was painted outdoors and her hat shades her eyes from the sun which is coming from her left. She has a rugged complexion and at this stage of her life, she appears to have few teeth. The impasto applied oil paint provides texture to the clothing. The foliage in the background is a riot of brushwork but to good effect. The portrait was painted at Mapledurham in 1933 but not exhibited until 1947 at the Royal Institute of Oil Painters.

title: Oxford from Headington Hill
subject: Landscape
blurb: This oil painting of Oxford from a garden on Headington Hill, early evening is in muted colours reflecting the time of day. There is a subtle blending and gradation of tones as the picture recedes into the lighter background as it is benefitting from the evening sunshine. This, like the majority of Knighton-Hammond’s work, would have been painted en plein air. The paint is applied thick leaving visible brushstrokes and thus texture.

title: A Circular Tower
subject: Landscape
blurb: A street scene with a circular tower. The depiction of the buildings within the streetscape are painted to perfection with regards to architectural detail and perspective. A couple of figures add a splash of colour and scale to the composition. A very fresh watercolour.

title: Derbyshire Dales
subject: Landscape
blurb: A landscape in the Derbyshire Dales was an early work of Knighton-Hammond who often made trips to the dales near Haddon Hall. A tranquil scene with a few sheep by some trees close to the river's edge. The river is spanned by a single arched bridge. There is a church beyond. The field in the foreground is naturally green in colour with the hills in the background being a blue/purple which is the colour created by the distance - the atmospheric colour.

title: Trees and figures overlooking the Mediterranean Sea
subject: Coastal Scene
blurb: This view overlooking the Mediterranean Sea was probably near Cap Martin just along the coast fom Menton. A vantage point chosen for the trees which make a statement in the composition. The figures add a splash of colour. One can almost feel the warmth of the sun and the sea breeze.

title: Father Christmas
subject: Portrait
blurb: A fun portrait of Father Christmas. The sitter is not recognisable so one has to assume it is the real deal! It may well have been a visitor to the house on 24 December who had time to sit for his portrait! Knighton-Hammond has captured the character of the sitter.

title: Flower Study
subject: Flower Study
blurb: This flower study was probably Knighton-Hammond amusing himself in his studio in later life. He has taken one of his third wife's arrangements, disturbed it by removing a few flowers and placing them on the table in front of the vase to make it less formal. The flowers are well painted and there is disposition of space between the blossoms.

title: Conversation piece with nudes
subject: Conversation Piece
blurb: The artrist has combined a family conversation piece with a study of nude women. Like all artists, studying in the life class was an essential element of training. The depiction of anatomy was perhaps the most challenging aspect for an artist. It was a subject in which Knighton-Hammond excelled. The figure studies here are freely painted in pure, direct watercolour with no underdrawing. He had the confidence to use the brush as an intrument of his draughtsmanship. The figures are fully focused and listen intensely to what is being said and the result of which is that it feels to the spectator that they are visually evesdropping on the conversation taking place.

title: French Riviera
subject: Streetscape
blurb: A scene somewhere along the French Riviera. The figures are going about their work by a wall provide the colour to the composition. The campanile dominates the picture rising out of the buildings. The architecture is depicted using very little detail but has a full effect.

title: Caravan and market, Menton
subject: Streetscape
blurb: A caravan and funfair in the market place in Menton. The figures and goats passing through the foreground give movement to the composition. These would have been sketched at lightning speed in pure, direct watercolour. The tall buildings are bathed in sunlight with the maritime alps beyond. There appears to be a colourful funfair in the market place and the trees add to the array of colours. The shadows are depicted in the Impressionist manner of not just colour with an absence of light but colour of a different value adding to the interest for the spectator.

title: I Gesuiti, Venice
subject: Church
blurb: Chiesa di Santa Maria Assunta, more commonly known as I Gesuiti, in Venice has a Baroque facade overlooking the Lagoon. A watercolour of great freedom yet great accuracy. The artist gives an impression of the architecture of the church and the buildings running beyond creating perspective and the scene is easily recognisable. The busy figures give an indication of the scale of the building and create great movement and fluidity. The water in the Lagoon reflects the buildings and boats to good effect.

title: A Canal in Venice
subject: Cityscape
blurb: On moving to the Continent in 1922, Knighton-Hammond initially travelled and stayed in Venice. It was an exciting time for him and he was busy painting and etching in the city. This canal scene is typically Venice with tall buildings flanking the narrow canal linked by the by an arched bridge. A gondolier in the foreground is either about to get into or out of his gondola. Other gondolas are travelling down the canal. With a few lines the artist is able to create a very easily readable composition

title: I Gesuiti, Venice
subject: Church
blurb: Chiesa di Santa Maria Assunta, more commonly known as I Gesuiti in Venice has a prominent Baroque facade overlooking the Lagoon. Knighton-Hammond features the buildings also overlooking the Lagoon and various sailing boats moored up and others out on the water. The architecture is cleverly detailed. It would appear that the etching is a reverse or mirror image so the artist did not reverse the image on the plate.

title: Salute, Venice
subject: Streetscape
blurb: Santa Maria della Salute in Venice is featured faintly in the background . The etching primarily focuses on the figures on the bridge spanning the canal. As with watercolour, Knighton-Hammond is able to achieve the same spontaneity when sketching with his etching needle. He uses the speed of the drawing to give the figures movement.

title: Tewkesbury Abbey
subject: Streetscape
blurb: The artist would have been positioned alongside the River Avon when he sketched the street scene with Tewkesbury Abbey. The river, cleverly depicted with a gentle flow, forms the foreground with historic buildings and the street leading to the view of the Abbey in the background. The horse and rider and figures in the street give movement to the composition. There is sufficient detail in the buildings for the architecture to be read.

title: Chetham's Hospital, Manchester
subject: Interior Scene
blurb: An impressive interior view of the Baronial Hall at Chetham's Hospital, Manchester. Steeped in medieval history the building dates back to the 15th century. The large inglenook fireplace is the focal point of the hall and was probably a later insertion. Knighton-Hammond picks out the historic architectural deatils and the clever hatching provides atmosphere to the interior. The figures give an idea of size and volume of the hall.

title: Flower Study
subject: Flower Study
blurb: Later in life Knighton-Hammond was still active in his studio often painting still life compositions. His third wife, Iris, was an accomplished flower arranger and would provide an arrangement in a vase in the studio. It was generally too formal for the artist and he would remove a few blossoms and place them on the table in front of the vase reducing the formality - much to his wife's annoyance! This appears to have been what happened with this arrangement painted in thick brightly coloured oil paints. The impasto technique provides texture to the composition giving a 3-D effect to the petals and leaves.

title: A Square in Menton
subject: Streetscape
blurb: The facade of the building within the square is part in sunlight and part in shade. The foreground figures have spontaneity and movement. The composition is created with thick, impasto oil paint applied to good effect.

title: The Scrumpers
subject: Landscape
blurb: A fun picture of children scrumping or helping the adults collect the apples from the trees. This would have been a very quick sketch with the etching needle onto the waxed copper plate. Detail is minimal with outlines only and very little hatching but the resulting picture tells the story.

title: Christies Auction Rooms
subject: Interior Scene
blurb: A busy auction room at Christies with the auctioneer conducting proceedings from the rostrum. There is a sense of a buzz going on in the room. Many of the figures have been created with very few lines yet one has a sense of realism without the detail.

title: Munitions Plant
subject: Industrial Scene
blurb: Knighton-Hammond was engaged by the Government and British Dyes during the First World War to illustrate the buildings and processes taking place as part of the war effort. This munitions plant shows Knighton-Hammond’s skilful draughtsmanship with perspective. A busy scene with workers going about their duties. A man is working from a ladder attaching lines to stabilise a pole which give an indication of scale. Light and shadow give a sense of atmosphere to the composition.

title: Epsom Downs, Derby Day
subject: Sporting Scene
blurb: This picture is a typical 'behind the scenes' view of the Epsom race meeting on Derby Day. The people had more appeal to Knighton-Hammond than the actual horses and jockeys. The artist has painted the back view of tents and fairground attractions with the spectator stands in the background. A busy and colourful picture in which the people are going about their business.

title: Village scene from the meadows
subject: Landscape
blurb: The village church and houses in the mid-foreground are framed by large trees. There are cattle in the field. A very freely drawn watercolour full of light and colour.

title: Huntsmen, hounds and bystanders, 1901
subject: Hunting Scene
blurb: This is a fun sporting picture probably painted on the kitchen table in 1901 whilst the artist was living in London. The huntsmen are passing through a gate onto the road. Children are attending the gate and two women are observing from the opposite side of the road. The hounds lead the way. These sporting pictures were produced by the artist along with picture postcards to help make a living at this period in his career.

title: Prestbury, June 1911
subject: Streetscape
blurb: This street scene painted in June 1911 is possibly of Prestbury Road, Prestbury. The Cheshire village appealed to the artist as he produced a number of watercolours of various streets. The buildings are well depicted giving an immediate appreciation of the architecture in the facades. The figures give scale and the shepherd driving his sheep along the road gives a sense of movement. The horse and cart at the side of the road shows a clever understanding of foreshortening. Picturesque Prestbury was one of a number of locations around Manchester where Adolphe Valette, Art Master at Manchester Municipal School of Art would bring students on open-air study trips. Knighton-Hammond studied under Valette so it may well have been on one of these trips that this picture was painted. It has signs of the influence of Valette who taught the ways of the Impressionists with regards to colour, light and freedom of brushwork.

title: Boats moored on a river
subject: Boating Scene
blurb: This river scene (possibly the Thames) is busy with boats in the background. The two rowing boats in the foreground are moored up. The river is calm and the picture has a degree of tranquility about it.

title: St Mary's Church, South Perrott
subject: Landscape
blurb: This watercolour demonstrates Knighton-Hammond's skill in the depiction of architecture. St Mary's Church is painted directly in watercolour with great freedom yet with great accuracy. One gets an impression of detail such as the tracery in the masonry windows sufficient for a full appreciation and understanding of the historic building. The thatched cottage and masonry boundary wall are of similar effect.

title: A Cheshire Pool, Bramhall
subject: Landscape
blurb: In this watercolour the artist demonstrates his skill in depicting foliage at the water's edge and in the trees. The cattle in the field and ducks on the water give movement to the composition. The local colour of the foreground contrasts with the atmospheric colours in the background.

title: Figures by a river
subject: Landscape
blurb: The focal points of this picture are the figures at the edge of the river. Sketched in pure direct watercolour at lightning speed there is movement and spontaneity. The river flowing through the valley draws the eye to the buildings at the foot of the mountains rising in the background. Simple colour washes with a limited palette painted to good effect.

title: The Harbour, San Remo
subject: Coastal Scene
blurb: This harbour scene is dominated by the bow of the sailing boat moored in the harbour at San Remo painted in 1924. Freely painted in direct watercolour, the mid-ground buildings have little architectural detail but the impression created is sufficiently well executed for one to immediately appreciate the white washed facades and terracotta roofs. The mountains in the background are painted in an atmospheric blue. The harbour is calm and gives off reflections of the boats in harbour.

title: Lake surrounded by hills with a rainbow
subject: Landscape
blurb: This landscape with a lake, hills and rainbow is freely painted in watercolours. With very little gradation of colour the artist cleverly achieves aerial perspective drawing the spectator's eye through the valley and beyond. The rainbow is a sweeping brushstroke with limited colour giving a mere impression or suggestion but one immediate knows extactly what it is.

title: Brine Well with 'A' Power Station
subject: Industrial Scene
blurb: Brine Well with 'A' Power Station in background, Dow Chemical Plant is a colourful oil painting. The striking vertical tower structure and the tall chimney stacks give a degree of majesty to an unlikely composition. The plant was built with no other purpose than to be functional yet through Knighton-Hammond's eyes he sees shape, line and space combined to bring order to the disorderly industrial scene. He transforms the function into form and creates a subject worthy of artistic interest. Reproduced by kind permission of the Herbert H and Grace A Dow Foundation.

title: The Dow Chemical Company Main Office Building, Midland, Michigan
subject: Industrial Scene
blurb: The Dow Chemical Company Main Office Building creates a delightful composition with the office building juxtaposed with the industrial plant in the background. It would appear to have been painted in the autumn as the trees are losing their leaves. The seasonal light and colour give the picture great depth and atmosphere. The people and early motor cars bring a human touch and scale to the composition. This is believed to have been one of Herbert Dow's favourite pictures by Knighton-Hammond. Mr Dow's car is half hidden in the portico area of the office building on the left. Reproduced by kind permission of the Herbert H and Grace A Dow Foundation.

title: Caustic Pot House
subject: Industrial Scene
blurb: The Caustic Pot House Caustic Soda Production, Dow Chemical Plant shows the shared interests between patron and artist. Both Herbert Dow and Knighton-Hammond could see great beauty and interest in these 'cathedrals' of industry. The artist found a good high-level vantage point, presumably on a gantry, from which to paint. The interior is depicted in subdued colours probably tinted by the processes taking place in the plant. Reproduced by kind permission of the Herbert H and Grace A Dow Foundation.

title: Epsom Salt Plant
subject: Industrial Scene
blurb: The Epsom Salt Plant was part of the Dow Chemical Plant in Midland, Michigan. Whilst in America, Knighton-Hammond worked predominently in oils, he did occasionally return to watercolours as for this picture. His work continues to have great freedom yet great accuracy. The composition is well selected and structured. The figures in the foregound and middle distance in the access road bring scale and movement to the picture. Reproduced by kind permission of the Herbert H and Grace A Dow Foundation.

title: Looking down the Tittabawassee River
subject: Industrial Scene
blurb: With Looking down the Tittabawassee River at the Dow Chemical Plant, Midland, Michigan Knighton-Hammond creates a composition of power and movement. The power coming from the giant chimney stacks discharging smoke into the atmosphere and dispersing into the clouds. The artist was able to demonstrate industry harmonising with nature. The chimneys with their tall vertical lines breaking across the horizon at different heights and distances, create without any artificiality an inherently dignified design. The painting has impressionistic qualities in terms of the application of the thick oil paint applied to canvas. Reproduced by kind permission of the Herbert H and Grace A Dow Foundation.

title: Sailing boats in harbour
subject: Coastal Scene
blurb: This composition is Knighton-Hammond working at great speed and with great freedom. Using pure, direct watercolour - no under drawing - he confidently depicts the elements of the picture - the architure in the background and the boats in the foreground - with little detail but one can immediately appreciate the impression being created.

title: Sailing boat being loaded
subject: Coastal Scene
blurb: A busy harbour scene with a sailing boat being loaded from a lorry. The figures are freely drawn and have great spontaneity giving movement as they go about their tasks.

title: Mary and her mother sitting on steps
subject: Streetscape
blurb: The main focus of the composition is Mary, the artist's daughter and her mother sitting on steps. The two figures are bathed in sunlight with shadows around them. A very freely drawn watercolour with good use of colour.

title: Farm buildings by a pond
subject: Landscape
blurb: A barn and cottages by a pond. The farmer is herding his cattle along the road towards the spectator. A fresh, bright and colourful early watercolour by the artist. There is clever reflections in the water and the foliage of the trees are particularly well executed.

title: Market in Menton
subject: Streetscape
blurb: A busy market scene with figures deep in conversation. A typical subject for Knighton-Hammond who loved painting streetscapes. He was able to bring the people to life with colour and movement.

title: Homewards for Christmas
subject: Streetscape
blurb: This wintery scene captures the bitterness of the weather and the movement of the coach and horses. The coach is passing through a town or village in late afternoon. The artist cleverly gives atmosphere and movement to the composition.

title: Burpham Court House, Guildford
subject: Landscape
blurb: This bold watercolour was given as a present to Ann Benson (who was later to become the artist's step-daughter) as indicated in the inscription 'To Ann, July 26th 1931'. Burpham Court House was owned by the Benson family. Knighton-Hammond was a friend of the family and on one of his visits he painted this impressive watercolour. He freely depicts the architectural details of the historic timber framed building to good effect. The facade is bathed in sunlight. The drive draws the spectators eye to the house.

title: Street in Old Town, San Remo
subject: Streetscape
blurb: Street in Old Town, San Remo was exhibited at the Beaux Art Gallery in London in 1924. The exhibition was entitled 'Venice and the Riviera' and received much attention as amongst the visitors were Queen Mary, Sir Joseph Duveen, Prince Nicholas and other members of the Greek Royal Family. The picture is framed through an arch and the street is lined with tall buildings. The people are busy going about their business in street. The figures have great movement and colour.

title: Landscape with valley and hills
subject: Landscape
blurb: River valley with hills in the background and corn stooks and figures in foreground.

title: Cattle and chickens on a roadway
subject: Landscape
blurb: The road way draws the spectator's eye towards the chicken and cattle in the farm setting.

title: Epsom
subject: Sporting Scene
blurb: This is a behind the action look at the race meeting. Knighton-Hammond was perhaps more interested in the people at race meetings than the actual racing! A colourful picture depicted in rich, impasto oil paints. One can almost hear the chatter of the people either celebrating their wins or commiserating their losses!

title: Staff Nurse Margaret Thomas
subject: Portrait
blurb: Staff Nurse Margaret Thomas nursed Knighton-Hammond when he was in Bridgwater Hospital in 1962. Staff Nurse Thomas attending four sittings in the artist's studio. The charming portrait was exhibited at the Royal Institute of Oil Painters under the title 'A ministering angel thou'. The portrait was widely reported in the national press. In a sympathetic study the artist has captured the nurse with an expression of caring dedication.

title: Pont Dwgan Mill, North Wales
subject: Landscape
blurb: This large impressive oil painting of Pont Dwgan Mill and bridge was an early work by Knighton-Hammond. The water fall in the background give a hint of the power of the water which via the mill race would turn the mill wheel. The mill is in a rugged setting probably during the Autumn period.

title: The Banqueting Hall, Haddon Hall
subject: Interior Scene
blurb: This watercolour of the historic Banqueting Hall at Haddon Hall may well have been a study for a series of postcards of Haddon. The ruggedness of the medieval interior with its timber panelling give a real sense of history.

title: Huntsmen chasing their quarry
subject: Hunting Scene
blurb: The main characters in this comic study are two huntsmen at full gallop chasing their quarry. This would have later been used for postcards.

title: Huntsmen at full gallop
subject: Hunting Scene
blurb: This is a comic scene of huntsmen at full gallop being surrounded by hounds. It is likely that this was a study which was later used for postcards.

title: Coach and horse
subject: Sporting Scene
blurb: This pencil drawing of a coach and horse was undertaken as a proprietary study for a later painting. Knighton-Hammond has made notes on the drawing for what colours to use. A quick, simple sketch but drawn to perfection.

title: Hunting Scene
subject: Hunting Scene
blurb: The huntsmen are leading the hounds in a procession. With them all heading in the direction of the spectator there is clever foreshorting for both riders and hounds.

title: Flower Market
subject: Streetscape
blurb: This flower market is typical of Knighton-Hammond with a riot of colours. The figures are busy chatting to each other giving life to the composition.

title: Santa Maria della Salute, Venice
subject: Streetscape
blurb: Santa Maria della Salute is silhouetted against a striking blue sky. The church and buildings are bathed in sunlight. The shadows follow the blue theme of the sky.

title: The Gardener's Cottage, Haddon Hall
subject: Landscape
blurb: The Gardener's Cottage on the Haddon estate is constructed in masonry with stone mullion windows, dressed stone quoins, copings, buttress and chimney. The roof is covered in stone slates. Clearly, this is a high-end build which attracted the attention of Knighton-Hammond. He captures the architectural features of the local vernacular cottage which are embellished by the colourful pot plants placed against the façade. Located in a wooded area was painted around the time Knighton-Hammond was living and working in the Youlgrave area c1906.

title: Portrait of a woman
subject: Portrait
blurb: This portrait shows Knighton-Hammond's skill with blending pastels to achieving the gradation of colour for the modelling of elements. The manages to keep the colours bright which can sometimes be lost in blending.

title: A Farmhouse
subject: Landscape
blurb: The farmhouse is set in the farmland with cattle grazing in the door step! This is a colourful early picture by Knighton-Hammond and one can observe he has a mastery of drawing with the perspective of the house drawn with great freedom but great accuracy.

title: Richmond Bridge
subject: Landscape
blurb: A tranquil setting with the bridge being the focal point of the composition. The cloud study rises above the bridge and the reflective water beneath in the foreground. Human presence is given by the people in the boats.

title: San Remo
subject: Streetscape
blurb: This colourful composition depicts lively figures going about their business in the historic part of the town. The buildings are part in sunshine and part shadow. Conversations are taking place between the clusters of figures. Knighton-Hammond would have painted this watercolour at lightning speed resulting in the spontaneity and movement.

title: The Teenager
subject: Portrait
blurb: As he settled into old age, K-H continued to enjoy painting portraits. He liked having local people around him and would regularly usher them into the studio to pose. The Teenager was probably from a local Somerset family. The soft pastels are cleverly graded to create contours with the modelling of the sensitive face. The sitter is at ease and looks happy to pose; one can imagine K-H entertaining her with anecdotes as he painted.

title: Notre Dame gargoyle
subject: Cityscape
blurb: Knighton-Hammond carried out a number of etchings featuring the gargoyles on Notre Dame. These symbolic protectors have a practical purpose in discharging the roof water away from the building fabric. The gargoyles are part of the rich decor and Knighton-Hammond could see sufficient beauty in them to draw them for his etchings.

title: Hunting Scene
subject: Hunting Scene
blurb: This is a fun picture showing the huntsmen and women at gallop going after thier quarry. This would have been an early picture possibly produced on the kitchen table to enable the rent to be paid - times were tough!

title: Marlow on Thames
subject: Landscape
blurb: This watercolour of Marlow would date from the early 1900s. The cloudless sky is giving a range of light, colour and in turn atmosphere to the composition. One can sense the movement of the River Thames cascading over the weir. Knighton-Hammond positioned himself near Marlow Lock to paint the scene with All Saints Church dominating the skyline. The band of buildings and trees are atmospheric in colour silhouetted against the sky. The reflections in the water pick out the lighter colours of yellows and greens and Knighton-Hammond conjured up subtle qualities in watercolour to evoke the brightness of the day. Apart from the weir there is a stillness in the mood created by this budding young artist. With the absence of human presence, he has managed to optimise this aesthetic response to nature.

title: The Ball Room, Haddon Hall
subject: Interior Scene
blurb: The interior of the Ball Room at Haddon Hall with its fine panelling is well illustrated by Knighton-Hammond during his early career.

title: The Chapel, Haddon Hall
subject: Interior Scene
blurb: The interior of the Chapel of this fine historic building is beautifully depicted by the artist. Knighton-Hammond spent a good deal of time at Haddon Hall in his early life.

title: La campagne autour de San Remo
subject: Landscape
blurb: An etching with figures and trees in the foreground with San Remo beyond.

title: Windsor Castle
subject: Landscape
blurb: An etching of Windsor Castle dominating the skyline.

title: Pont Neuf, Paris
subject: Cityscape
blurb: Figures working under the arch of this famous bridge in the centre of Paris.

title: Flower Market, Menton
subject: Streetscape
blurb: A busy market scene flanked by the tall buildings forming the square. Freely drawn with the brush making for a very spontaneous composition.

title: Santa Maria della Salute, Venice
subject: Cityscape
blurb: The basilica of Santa Maria della Salute dominates the canal scene.

title: A Cottage by a pond
subject: Landscape
blurb: A pencil sketch of a cottage by a pond.

title: The Meet at the Old Hall
subject: Hunting Scene
blurb: The gathering of the hunt outside the entrance to the Old Hall. A colourful and lively picture.

title: The Port at Menton
subject: Coastal Scene
blurb: The figures are busy unloading the boat in the harbour. A typically fluent work from this period.

title: A Fifeshire Fishing Village
subject: Coastal Scene
blurb: A harbour scene with the tide out. The buildings beyond the harbour wall set the scene.

title: An Evening in Spring, Woodford, Cheshire
subject: Landscape
blurb: Cattle in a field with cottage in background. This is an early work showing Knighton-Hammond's skills as a romantic landscape painter.

title: Kings Street Knutsford
subject: Streetscape
blurb: This drawing of King Street in the market town of Knutsford has the Gaskell Memorial Tower dominating scene. The street is given depth by good prespective and the architecture is well executed. The figures give a sense of scale and life.

title: Nathaniel Brayne
subject: Portrait
blurb: Nathaniel Brayne was handiman to the Knighton-Hammond family in Ditchling. The portrait in pastels was used to illustrate the art of pastel painting for a series of articles on the subject for The Artist Magazine in 1940-41. The portrait is an example of the skill of pastel painting and how the artist creates soft lines and blends the colours to model the head and clothing.

title: A Market in the South of France
subject: Streetscape
blurb: In this complex, multi-figural composition in the busy market shows the artist taking advantage of the texture of paint using thick impasto to evoke reflections of shimmering light and intensity of colour. His love of engaging with everyday subjects and collective activity is clear in this composition. One can almost hear the conversations taking place in the hustle and bustle of the market which can be described as a celebration of urban life with the element of spontaneity has been fully integrated into the artistic process. The architecture is very dominant, powerfully emblematic and is bathed in sunlight. The linear perspective and the brilliant rendition of the materials of the façade are supremely executed. Knighton-Hammond worked predominantly in watercolours during his time working on the continent but this is an example of his undoubted skill in oils and in the understanding of the dynamics of urban life on the Franco Italian riviera in an Impressionist style.

title: A Street in Nevers, France
subject: Streetscape
blurb: Knighton-Hammond set himself up in the Rue de la Cathedrale in Nevers to execute this watercolour. The tower and the main body of the Cathedral St Cyr Ste Julitte is visible at the end of the street. The building with the turret is on the corner of Rue de la Cathedrale and Rue Albert Morlon. Without being slavish to detail, the architecture is skilfully depicted. The linear perspective shows off his draughtsmanship. The use of colour, light and tone have all the qualities and techniques of the Impressionists whom I greatly admired. The figures looked to have been painted with great freedom and speed giving spontaneity and movement.

title: Peveril Castle, Castleton, Derbyshire
subject: Landscape
blurb: Peveril Castle, Castleton in Derbyshire is high up in the Peak District. The castle is viewed through the gorge. The rugged terrain in this etching cleverly has aerial perspective giving a sense of depth to the gorge. This etching is one of a number of states of the subject as is likely to the the last state due to the amount of ink in the composition.

title: Jacobean Building in Ludlow
subject: Streetscape
blurb: A pencil drawing entitled 'A Jacobean Porch, Ludlow' is a fine architectural study. The artist has a mastery of perspective and draftsmanship. He gives scale to the composition with the figures in the street.

title: Marlow 1903
subject: Streetscape
blurb: A proprietary pencil drawing of a boy with a hand cart. The artist has made notes of the colours of various items in the composition which would have been the subject of a later watercolour or oil painting.

title: Conversation piece with 4 figures
subject: Conversation Piece
blurb: This pencil sketch would have been produced at lightning speed. Recording the figures going about their everyday lives would give the artist the confidence to sketch in this figure in his watercolour paintings using the brush only. Rarely do you observe any underdrawing in Knighton-Hammond's work. These clusters of figures can be seen in the streets or the harbourside in many of the artist's works

title: Conversation piece with 5 figures
subject: Conversation Piece
blurb: This drawing would have been produced within seconds. Rapid annotation of the figures in conversation would have given the artist the confidence to sketch out similar figures in his compositions with the brush with direct watercolour.

title: Conversation piece
subject: Conversation Piece
blurb: A quick sketch in charcoal of figure outside a caravan whilst Knighton-Hammond was waiting. He rarely missed the opportunity to sketch figures going about their daily lives.

title: Broad Street, Ludlow
subject: Streetscape
blurb: Pencil drawing of the Butter Cross at the head of Broad Street in Ludlow. A finely drawn architectural study which was later transferred to the etching plate.

title: High Street, Prestbury
subject: Landscape
blurb: The artist cleverly depicts the different styles of architecture in the high street in Prestbury, Cheshire. The buildings are bathed in sunlight with figure in the street which is picked out with a dappled light effect. Picturesque Prestbury was one of a number of locations around Manchester where Adolphe Valette, Art Master at Manchester Municipal School of Art would bring students on open-air study trips. Knighton-Hammond studied under Valette so it may well have been on one of these trips that this picture was painted. It has the signs of the influence of Valette who taught the ways of the Impressionists with regards to colour, light and freedom of brushwork.

title: Landscape
subject: Landscape
blurb: Landscape with shepherd driving his sheep.

title: Banqueting Hall, Haddon Hall
subject: Interior Scene
blurb: Interior of the Banqueting Hall at Haddon Hall in Derbyshire from the Academy series of postcard etchings. The grand interior of the Banqueting Hall.

title: Ball Room, Haddon Hall
subject: Interior Scene
blurb: From the Academy seriesof postcard etchings. Interior of the Ball Room at Haddon Hall in Derbyshire.

title: I'm Off
subject: Sporting Scene
blurb: A humourous hunting scene 'I'm Off' published by Raphael Tuck & Sons 'In the Hunting Fields' series 6079

title: The Old Love and the New
subject: Motoring Scene
blurb: 'The Old Love and the New' published by Raphael Tuck & Sons Motor Series No 6631. A coach and horse being overtaken by a motor car.

title: In the Country
subject: Sporting Scene
blurb: In the Country - The Carrier's Cart. A cert and two horses about to pick up a woman from The Carrier's Arms. From the 'Ellanbee' Coaching Series No 122

title: A lake in France
subject: Landscape
blurb: Figures by the side of a lake in France. A very fluid watercolour and the figure gives Knighton-Hammond the opportunity to use red in his composition.

title: Sisteron, France
subject: Landscape
blurb: This extensive, atmospheric landscape would have been encountered when Knighton-Hammond was on his travels around France. Inspired by new locations clearly added to the development of his style. To give depth to the composition the artist uses a series of horizontal planes. The buildings and foliage in the foreground are separated by the row of cypress trees from the landscape. The foreground is painted in pale greens, the local colour. As the picture recedes to the background the veil of atmosphere through which the distance is viewed turns the colours to blues – the atmospheric colour. This panoramic landscape is very responsive to light and colour with loose, freer and rhythmic brushwork applied at speed.

title: Olive Woods at Menton
subject: Landscape
blurb: A hazy blue picture with Old Town Menton in the background viewed from Olive Woods. The two figures in the mid-foreground give scale to the large trees.

title: Sailing Boats at Oneglia
subject: Coastal Scene
blurb: Two large sailing boats moored in the harbour at Oneglia. The sea looks choppy, and the harbour is flanked by a number of tall buildings.

title: Portrait of a Woman
subject: Portrait
blurb: All of Knighton-Hammond’s portraits have individuality conveying human presence as well as artistic process. With this portrait in profile there is a suggestion of emotional transitions and movement in what is normally the static genre of portrait painting. The artist has used thick, impasto paint to convey the volume of the head and give texture to the flesh and clothing. The plain background cleverly projects the sitter into the space of the spectator. .

title: Portrait of a Man
subject: Portrait
blurb: The sitter for this portrait is not known but is finely painted. The complexion is created by adding paint colours which optically mix when viewed from a distance. The portrait is of a thoughful, sensitive character study pepicting human presence rather than just artistic process.

title: The Ditchling Postman
subject: Portrait
blurb: The Ditchling Postman was Joseph Faulkner. Here depicted in his uniform and was probably at the end of his round when Knighton-Hammond invited him into the studio to sit for his portrait. This was not unusual as Knighton-Hammond enjoyed painting the characters of the town. Joe looks very much at ease and portrays his character communicated by his eyes. One can imagine sitter and artists were great friends and Joe would have been a regular visitor to the house if not the studio - although this is one of at least two portraits of Joe. The complexion of the sitter is created using the impasto technique.

title: Portrait of a Young Girl
subject: Portrait
blurb: Knighton-Hammond produced a portrait of a young woman with sensitive eyes who has the appearance of being deliberately very still to aid the artist. A rich, colourful example of the artist's great skill in producing not only a good likeness but also emotion and character.

title: Anne of Cleeve's House
subject: Streetscape
blurb: The historic Anne of Cleve's House in Ditchling is viewed from the church yard on the opposite side of West Street. The house was given to her by Henry VIII but was supposedly never occupied by her. The timber-framed section of the building dates from the 16th century. Knighton-Hammond would have enjoyed depicting the different periods of architecture and its details. There are grave stones in the foreground from where the artist had set up his easel.

title: The Butter Cross from Harp Lane, Ludlow
subject: Streetscape
blurb: The Butter Cross, Ludlow can be seen at the end of the narrow Harp Lane. The historic buildings channel the view of the focal point of this important building. The architecture is well depicted and demonstrates Knighton-Hammond's great skill in drawing details. The figures at the end of the street gives an idea of scale.

title: Hollyhocks
subject: Flower Study
blurb: The hollyhocks are a riot of colour dominating the foreground. The buildings in the background are likely to be in Menton.

title: The Dolomites
subject: Landscape
blurb: A very quick sketch with a limited reange of pastels, Knighton-Hammond creates an atmosphere of cold silence. The pastel was applied at great speed in an almost attacking style for the mountain range. The cloud study is much softer.

title: Cottage at Woodford
subject: Landscape
blurb: Plum Blossom Cottage at Woodford was a favourite location for Knighton-Hammond. This early watercolour is remarkable for its apparent naturalism. The timber framed, thatched cottage with its stucco finish is bathed in sunlight. The foliage of the trees is descriptive of observed natural, rich in form and colour with a profusion of constructive brushstrokes. The foreground leads the eye of the spectator to the cottage door where mother and child bring a human and sensitive touch to the composition.

title: Royal Exchange, Manchester
subject: Streetscape
blurb: The Royal Exchange, Manchester is a study of classical architecture. Horses and carts line up possibly delivering building materials for the construction taking place. A master class of perspective drawing.

title: Waterloo Bridge
subject: Cityscape
blurb: Waterloo Bridge is a combination of river and sky with the bridge and adjacent buildings at the intersection. There are boats in the moorings. The cloud study was of great interest and Knighton-Hammond studied the cloud studies of John Constable at the Tate. He was adept at the rapid notation required in capturing the ever changing sky.

title: Lewes Road/West Street, Ditchling
subject: Streetscape
blurb: Knighton-Hammond lived in Ditchling during the 1930s. The town was a haven for artists including Sir Frank Brangwyn who was a good friend. The street scene of Lewes Road and West Street depicts Ditchling's historic buildings and is busy with figures going about their business in the street.

title: Alton High Street
subject: Streetscape
blurb: Alton High Street was painted soon after Knighton-Hammond returned from Cap Martin in 1932 and is one of two similar pictures - the other is in the Curtis Museum in Alton. The architecture is painted with great freedom and great accuracy. The spectator's eye navigates the high street through the draw of perspective. A colourful picture enlivened by the figures going about their business in the street.

title: A Street in Menton
subject: Streetscape
blurb: A street scene in Old Town Menton. The street is narrow and flanked by tall buildings with one side bathed in sunlight and the other in shadow. The architecture and perspective are very finely depicted and the figures give life to the composition.

title: Threshing
subject: Landscape
blurb: This watercolour was exhibited at The Royal Institute of Painters in Watercolours in 1946. There is a buzz about this scene with the figures going about their duties to service the threshing machine.

title: Casino, Monte Carlo
location: Monte Carlo, Monte Carlo, Monte Carlo
subject: Streetscape
blurb: This early evening scene of the Casino in Monte Carlo is cleverly depicted with artificial light creating a very moody atmosphere. The figures have great movement and spontaneity and would have been painted at lightning speed.

title: Sunflowers
subject: Flower Study
blurb: Knighton-Hammond enjoyed painting flowers especially in later life. Here he has sunflowers in a blue vase and some loose on the table. Painted with great freedom and speed.

title: Wells Cathedral
subject: Streetscape
blurb: A view of Wells Cathedral in evening light after a wet day. Knighton-Hammond's etchings demonstrate his draftsmanship skills and the clever use of the distribution of the ink on the etching plate to produce different intensities of light and shadow.

title: The Family Outing
subject: Family Gathering
blurb: The artist's family on an outing in their caravan. Mrs Knighton-Hammond would do the driving when they went on family holidays around the country in the 1930s. The children are busy reading shaded from the sun with their floppy hats. The picture is a riot of colour developed whilst Knighton-Hammond lived on the Continent during the 1920s and early 30s.

title: Portrait of Monica Baber
subject: Portrait
blurb: The portrait of Monica Baber may well have been undertaken when Knighton-Hammond had a studio in London during the 1930s. It would appear to be a commissioned portrait painted in oils. Monica is shown with her left hand on her cheek in a thoughtful pose. The spectator's eyes are drawn to her eyes. The impasto technique gives great texture to her clothes. A rich portrait in colours and character.

title: Derwent Hall
subject: Landscape
blurb: Knighton-Hammond was commissioned by the FitzAlan family to produce a series of watercolours in and around Derwent Hall in Derbyshire. The mail purpose was to record the house and grounds before they were lost under a proposed reservoir. This elevation of Derwent Hall is set in the formal gardens. The architecture is drawn with fine perspective as the spectator's eye is navigated along the facade to the trees in the rising background.

title: The Entrance at Derwent Hall
subject: Landscape
blurb: Knighton-Hammond was commissioned by the FitzAlan family to a series of watercolours in and around Derwent Hall in Derbyshire. The main purpose was to record the house and grounds before they were lost under the proposed reservoir. The grand gated entrance to the hall from the informal garden has elegance and contextual harmony with the rolling hills beyond.

title: A caravan and haystack in landscape
subject: Landscape
blurb: The caravan and hay rick are front and centre in this landscape. Knighton-Hammond shows his virtuosity with the use of thick oil paint giving texture, in particular to the straw in the rick and the surrounding grass. The caravan and wagon are drawn with great precision yet with great freedom.

title: Old Hall, Youlgrave
subject: Landscape
blurb: Old Hall dominates the composition with beautifully depicted vernacular architect of Derbyshire. The picture is brought to life with the sheep ambling along the street and a young girl at play with her hoop.

title: Haddon Hall, Derbyshire
subject: Landscape
blurb: The etching shows the great house dominating the background elevated proudly with a river in the foreground passing under a bridge. A large tree dominates the centre ground. Knighton-Hammond was a frequent visitor to Haddon Hall from early in his career. He enjoyed drawing and painting in the grounds.

title: Flower Market, Menton
subject: Streetscape
blurb: A busy flower market with the figures nestled amongst the trees and umbrellas. Soft pastel colours depict the buildings forming the backdrop.

title: Boats at Concarneau
subject: Coastal Scene
blurb: Harbour scene with sailing boats and figures in conversation standing on the harbour wall. A colourful watercolour produced at lightning speed as was Knighton-Hammond's way with a watercolour brush in hand.

title: Pasture scene with hay stacks and figures
subject: Landscape
blurb: A sunbathed pasture with figures (possibly the artist's family) amongst haystacks with a windmill in the background on a hill. This watercolour would have been painted at great speed by the artist giving spontaneity to the composition.

title: Concarneau, Brittany
subject: Coastal Scene
blurb: This etching depicts fishermen on the harbourside with boats in the background. The etching shows Knighton-Hammond's draughtsmanship skills where he is able to create aerial perspective giving the disposition of space with little in the way of structure.

title: Hyde Park Corner
subject: Landscape
blurb: This etching by Knighton-Hammond depects figures seated below a tree in parkland setting with buildings beyond. Done during the winter as can be seen by the tree without its leaves.

title: Boats in the Harbour in Menton
subject: Coastal Scene
blurb: The boats in the harbour and the architecture of old town Menton have been painted in vibrant colours. Thick impasto oil paint gives so much texture to the composition. This painting was one of two featured on the Antiques Road Show at Southwell Minster on 26th October 2008.

title: The Dairyman
subject: Portrait
blurb: Knighton-Hammond captures the Dairyman as he exits the dairy. Milking is still going on in the background. Another character which the artist would have enjoyed painting. He has used thick oil paint with an impasto technique. The paint gives texture to the face and clothing. The artist has given great movement to the figure captured with arrested motion.

title: Carter (Mr Frank Hole)
subject: Portrait
blurb: Mr Frank Hole or Carter as he was known work on a local farm close to Knighton-Hammond home and studio in Seaborough in Dorset. Painted in impasto this is very much a character study harping back to Knighton-Hammond's days in Ditchling during the 1930s. There is great sensitivity with the sitter's eyes and power in his hands. The face and its complexion are built up with juxtaposed colours relying on optical mixing keeping the colours fresh. One has the feeling that Knighton-Hammond would have enjoyed painting Frank's portrait and would have got on well with the sitter.

title: Portrait of Emmeline Hammond
subject: Portrait
blurb: A sensitive portrait of the artist's second wife Emmeline or more affectionately known as May. During the late 1920s and early 30s Knighton-Hammond's wife and daughter, Mary, featured in much of his work. In this portrait human presence was equal to artistic process with May being give a thoughtful, sensitive pose.

title: A Dunkirk Soldier
subject: Portrait
blurb: Knighton-Hammond has captured the expression of a soldier who has been through the trauma of war. The stress is still in the face. The subtle tone gives the spectator a sombreness of the feelings still within the soldier. The soldier’s eyes are quite haunting from what they had witnessed.

title: A Sussex Farmer
subject: Portrait
blurb: The Sussex Farmer was Mr Holman of Ditchling. The portrait was exhibited at the Royal Academy in 1938 and had the prestige of being hung ‘on the line’. The portrait exemplifies Knighton-Hammond’s skills with character studies conveying human presence rather than artistic process. The rugged face and strong hands are boldly depicted in thick impasto oil paint. The old characters were to feature in many of Knighton-Hammond’s portraits whilst he lived at Ditchling showing his penetrating powers of observation. A Sussex Farmer was one of two paintings featured on The Antiques Road Show at Southwell Minster on 26th October 2008.

title: Cypress & Olive Trees, Menton
subject: Landscape
blurb: Cypress & Olives, Menton has a row of tree regimentally aligned before town visible in the gaps sketched out in watercolour in a very free manner. Figures are going about their business in the foreground in the usual and colourful Knighton-Hammond way. The picture had the honour of being exhibited in the Central Gallery of the Paris Salon in 1927.

title: Figures in a Field of Haystacks
subject: Landscape
blurb: The figures in the foreground of the field have been quickly sketched giving them life and spontaneity. The field with the corn stooks is bathed in bright sunlight apart from the area of shadow cast by the tree. The shadow has been depicted, not with an absence of light, but in a colour of a different value. This technique follows the impressionist style the artist would have picked up whilst working on the continent.

title: Battersea Power Station
subject: Cityscape
blurb: Battersea Power Station on the horizon is silhouetted in the sky along with the bridge. Pastel painting provides a technique for creating very atmospheric compositions. The boats in the foreground have stronger colour and definition contrasting with the background shrouded in a vail of atmosphere.

title: London Bridge
subject: Cityscape
blurb: London Bridge was painted on a dull day. A variety of boats are moored on the quayside and were clearly painted at great speed and with great confidence directly with the brush. No under-drawing being visible. The gloomy day has created a vail of atmosphere to the bridge on the horizon in the background.

title: The Ligurian Alps from the Nervia Valley
blurb: The Torrente Nervia runs through an expansive valley with the village on the far side at the foot of the Alps. There are figures at the near side at the river’s edge adding the usual human touch and scale to the expansive composition with the dominant blue of the river.

title: Cathedral at Le Puy
subject: Landscape
blurb: The Cathedral at Le Puy dominates the street scene. The buildings leading to the cathedral are observed in sunlight and shadow. The figures in the street provide movement and spontaneity to the composition. This is another fine example of the artist’s mastery of depicting architectural form.

title: Sospel in the Maritime Alps
subject: Landscape
blurb: The Roman Bridge at Sospel is bathed in sunlight with the Alps in the background. The artist depicts the architecture with minimal detailing relying on the overall impression created which allows the spectator to read the form. Typical Knighton-Hammond pastel colours have been used to great effect. This is very much painted in the manner of the Impressionists who were painters of light, water and colour - all present here. Also, observe the shadow, which was not an absence of light, but light of a different quality and of different value. The old bridge dates from the 13th century and was used by travellers to cross the River Bevera. It was bombed during WWII but restored after.

title: Castellane near Grasse
subject: Streetscape
blurb: The old Inn at Castellane near Grasse is in rich in sunlight and shadow. Knighton-Hammond uses dappled sunlight created by the dominant tree to good effect exploiting the special ability of watercolour to convey light and space. The street scene has cattle are being driven on the pavement past the inn with its arches making up the facade of the of the building. People in the street and in the inn observe the procession. The figure in red is a feature of the artist giving a splash of vibrancy to the composition. When Knighton-Hammond portrays everyday life, he cleverly elevated it into an art form.
